17743-rosemary-a-christmas-story.title: A Christmas Story
17743-rosemary-a-christmas-story.creator: C. N. and A. M. WILLIAMSON
17743-rosemary-a-christmas-story.description: A book by C. N. and A. M. WILLIAMSON. It would be Christmas soon, and he thought that he would rather get it over on the Riviera than anywhere else, because the blue and gold weather would not remind him of other Christmases which were gone--pure, white, cold Christmases, musical with joy-bells and sweet with aromatic pine, the scent of trees born to be Christmas trees.

arxiv-1903-07570.title: Measurements of top-quark pair spin correlations in the e ​ μ e\mu channel at s = 13 \sqrt{s}=13 TeV using p ​ p pp collisions in the ATLAS detector
arxiv-1903-07570.description: Abstract A measurement of observables sensitive to spin correlations in t ​ t ¯ t\bar{t} production is presented, using 36.1 fb -1 of p ​ p pp collision data at s = 13 \sqrt{s}=13 TeV recorded with the ATLAS detector at the Large Hadron Collider.

arxiv-1911-03045.title: On approximating the shape of one dimensional functions
arxiv-1911-03045.creator: Chaitanya Joshi, Paul T. Brown, Stephen Joe
arxiv-1911-03045.description: Abstract Consider an s s -dimensional function being evaluated at n n points of a low discrepancy sequence (LDS), where the objective is to approximate the one-dimensional functions that result from integrating out ( s − 1 ) (s-1) variables. Here, the emphasis is on accurately approximating the shape of such one-dimensional functions.

arxiv-2207-06315.title: Transition to turbulence in nonuniform coronal loops driven by torsional Alfvén waves.
arxiv-2207-06315.creator: Sergio Díaz-Suárez, Roberto Soler
arxiv-2207-06315.description: Abstract It has been shown in a previous work that torsional Alfvén waves can drive turbulence in nonuniform coronal loops with a purely axial magnetic field. Here we explore the role of the magnetic twist. We modeled a coronal loop as a transversely nonuniform straight flux tube, anchored in the photosphere, and embedded in a uniform coronal environment.

arxiv-2208-07214.title: Improved Numerical Scheme for the Generalized Kuramoto Model
arxiv-2208-07214.creator: Hyun Keun Lee, Hyunsuk Hong, Joonhyun Yeo
arxiv-2208-07214.description: Abstract We present an improved and more accurate numerical scheme for a generalization of the Kuramoto model of coupled phase oscillators to the three-dimensional space. The present numerical scheme relies crucially on our observation that the generalized Kuramoto model corresponds to particles on the unit sphere undergoing rigid body rotations with position-dependent angular velocities.

arxiv-2212-03039.title: Covariance Regularization for Probabilistic Linear Discriminant Analysis
arxiv-2212-03039.creator: Zhiyuan Peng, Mingjie Shao, Xuanji He, Xu Li, Tan Lee, Ke Ding, Guanglu Wan
arxiv-2212-03039.description: Abstract Probabilistic linear discriminant analysis (PLDA) is commonly used in speaker verification systems to score the similarity of speaker embeddings. Recent studies improved the performance of PLDA in domain-matched conditions by diagonalizing its covariance. We suspect such brutal pruning approach could eliminate its capacity in modeling dimension correlation of speaker embeddings, leading to inadequate performance with domain adaptation.

arxiv-2304-13430.title: The Logic of Logic Programming
arxiv-2304-13430.creator: Marc Denecker, David S. Warren
arxiv-2304-13430.description: Abstract Our position is that logic programming is not programming in the Horn clause sublogic of classical logic, but programming in a logic of (inductive) definitions . Thus, the similarity between prototypical Prolog programs (e.g., member, append, …) and how inductive definitions are expressed in mathematical text, is not coincidental but essential.

arxiv-2307-13019.title: Fixed point results for Prešić type contractive mappings in b b -metric spaces
arxiv-2307-13019.creator: Talat Nazir, Sergei Silvestrov
arxiv-2307-13019.description: Abstract The fixed point results for generalized Prešić type mappings in the setup of b b -metric spaces are obtained. The stability of fixed point set of Prešić type mappings is also established. Several examples are also presented to illustrate the validity of the main results.

arxiv-2311-08717.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Khushdil Ahmad 1, Eric R Dolores-Cuenca 2 4 ∗ {}^{2}{}^{4}*, Khurram Shabbir 3. We apply operad theory to enumerative combinatorics in order to count the number of shuffles between series-parallel posets and chains. arxiv-2403-10545.title: The role of fluid friction in streamer formation and biofilm growth
arxiv-2403-10545.creator: Cornelius Wittig 1 , Michael Wagner 2 , Romain Vallon 1 , Thomas Crouzier 3 , Wouter van der Wijngaart 4 , Harald Horn 5 , and Shervin Bagheri 1
arxiv-2403-10545.description: Abstract Bacillus subtilis biofilms were grown in laminar channel flow at wall shear stress spanning one order of magnitude ( τ w = 0.068 Pa \tau_{w}=$0.068\text{\,}\mathrm{Pa}$ to τ w = 0.67 Pa \tau_{w}=$0.67\text{\,}\mathrm{Pa}$ ). We monitor, non-invasively, the evolution of the three-dimensional distribution of biofilm over seven days using optical coherence tomography (OCT).

arxiv-2502-00557.title: Sampling Binary Data by Denoising through Score Functions
arxiv-2502-00557.creator: ​​​​​ Francis Bach Saeed Saremi
arxiv-2502-00557.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by ​​​​​ Francis Bach Saeed Saremi. Gaussian smoothing combined with a probabilistic framework for denoising via the empirical Bayes formalism, i.e., the Tweedie-Miyasawa formula (TMF), are the two key ingredients in the success of score-based generative models in Euclidean spaces. Smoothing holds the key for easing the problem of learning and sampling in high dimensions, denoising is needed for recovering the original signal, and TMF ties these together via the score function of noisy data.

arxiv-2502-03145.title: Error Scaling of Sea Quark Isospin-Breaking Effects
arxiv-2502-03145.creator: Paola Tavella
arxiv-2502-03145.description: Abstract Sea-quark isospin-breaking effects (IBE) are difficult to compute since they require the evaluation of all-to-all propagators. However, the quest for high-precision calculations motivates a detailed study of these contributions. There are strong arguments that the stochastic error associated with these quantities should diverge in the continuum and infinite-volume limit, resulting in a possible bottleneck for the method.

arxiv-2503-10809.title: MIP against Agent: Malicious Image Patches Hijacking Multimodal OS Agents
arxiv-2503-10809.creator: Lukas Aichberger Alasdair Paren Guohao Li Philip Torr Yarin Gal Adel Bibi
arxiv-2503-10809.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Lukas Aichberger Alasdair Paren Guohao Li Philip Torr Yarin Gal Adel Bibi. Recent advances in operating system (OS) agents have enabled vision-language models (VLMs) to directly control a user’s computer. Unlike conventional VLMs that passively output text, OS agents autonomously perform computer-based tasks in response to a single user prompt. OS agents do so by capturing, parsing, and analysing screenshots and executing low-level actions via application programming interfaces (APIs), such as mouse clicks and keyboard inputs.

arxiv-2601-18400.title: On the Bandwidth Consumption of Blockchains
arxiv-2601-18400.creator: Andrei Lebedev, Vincent Gramoli
arxiv-2601-18400.description: Abstract With the advent of blockchain technology, the number of proposals has boomed. The network traffic imposed by these blockchain proposals increases the cost of hosting nodes. Unfortunately, as of today, we are not aware of any comparative study of the bandwidth consumption of blockchains. In this paper, we propose the first empirical comparison of blockchain bandwidth consumption.

pmc-10596947.title: Barriers and enablers to vaccine uptake in the Ultra-Orthodox Jewish population: a systematic review
pmc-10596947.creator: A Jacobson, S Spitzer, Y Gorelik, M Edelstein
pmc-10596947.description: BackgroundThe Jewish Ultra-Orthodox (UO) population is an undervaccinated minority group that has been disproportionally affected by outbreaks of vaccine-preventable diseases (VPD) such as measles and polio. Underlying reasons remain poorly characterized. We aimed to identify vaccination barriers and enablers in this population.

pmc-10632917.title: Social Presence, Negative Emotions, and Self-Protective Behavioral Intentions of Nonsmokers in Response to Secondhand Smoking in Virtual Reality: Quasi-Experimental Design
pmc-10632917.creator: Miao Liu, Yicheng Zhu, Zihan Xu, Sitong Meng, Gunther Eysenbach, Tiffany Leung, Zexin Ma, Inci Derya Yucel
pmc-10632917.description: BackgroundThe application of virtual reality (VR) in health care has grown rapidly in China, where approximately half of the population is directly exposed to secondhand smoke (SHS). As VR headsets have become increasingly popular and short video platforms have incorporated 360° videos in China, new formats and opportunities for health campaigns about SHS have emerged.

pmc-11667745.title: Evaluating Resonant Acoustic Mixing as a Wet Granulation Process
pmc-11667745.creator: Matthew
pmc-11667745.description: Control of powder properties is crucial for industrial processes across the food, pharmaceutical, agriculture, and mineral processing industries, and granulation is an important tool for providing agglomerated particles with controllable properties. However, existing granulation processes are not readily integrated with other processing steps and are not appropriate for some types of materials.

pmc-11713033.title: ApoE4 antibody ameliorates cognitive impairments and synapse loss in ApoE4/Tau‐P301S mice
pmc-11713033.creator: Ha‐Lim Song, Min‐Seok Kim, Mi‐Hyang Cho, Yeon‐Seon Mun, Na‐Young Kim, Jung‐Su Shin, Jun‐Sub Kim, Dong‐Hou Kim, Seung‐Yong Yoon
pmc-11713033.description: BackgroundThe Apolipoprotein E4 isoform (ApoE4), encoded by the APOE gene, stands out as the most influential genetic factor in late‐onset Alzheimer’s disease (LOAD). The ApoE4 isoform contributes to metabolic and neuropathological abnormalities during brain aging, with a strong correlation observed in APOE4‐positive Alzheimer’s disease cases between phosphorylated tau burden and amyloid deposition.

pmc-12402190.title: MAIA platform for routine clinical testing: an artificial intelligence embryo selection tool developed to assist embryologists
pmc-12402190.creator: Mariana Nicolielo, Catherine Kuhn Jacobs, Bruna Lourenço, Murilo Costa Maffeis, Dóris Spinosa Chéles, Matheus Búbola Duarte, Bruno Araújo Mendes, Vinícius Casado Moraes, Maurício Barbour Chehin, José Roberto Alegretti, Eduardo Leme Alves da Motta, Aline Rodrigues Lorenzon, Marcelo Fábio Gouveia Nogu
pmc-12402190.description: The need to reduce the number of embryos transferred in assisted reproductive care to prevent multiple gestations has led to a stronger emphasis on selecting embryos with the highest morphological quality. Although this evaluation has traditionally been performed by trained embryologists, the increasing use of time-lapse incubators has introduced a greater volume of data and subjectivity in decision-making.

pmc-12589404.title: Physiological and yield responses of Camelina sativa to modified Biochar under drought stress
pmc-12589404.creator: Azra Noreen, Summera Jahan, Atif Kamran, Abeer Hashem, Graciela Dolores Avila-Quezada, Elsayed Fathi Abd-Allah
pmc-12589404.description: Water stress is the most crucial abiotic stress, adversely affecting soil productivity and global food production. The soil productivity can be enhanced by utilizing organic soil conditioners such as organically modified sugarcane bagasse biochar (ASBB) which can potentially enhance crop yield. On the other hand, Pakistan’s domestic edible oil production is notably insufficient.

pmc-12748834.title: Comparative analysis of key phytochemicals and biological activities of Tartary buckwheat and Flos Sophorae Immaturus
pmc-12748834.creator: Lang Xu, Tanzim Jahan, Yu Wang, Bingqing Wang, Md Nurul Huda, Wei Li, Dili Lai, Junqiang Zhou, Wan Tang, Dujuan Shi, Qiang Yang, Fan Zhang, Baoping Zhao, Zhiyuan Chen, Meiliang Zhou
pmc-12748834.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Flavonoids such as rutin, quercetin, and kaempferol are the major bioactive compounds in Tartary buckwheat (TB) and Flos Sophorae Immaturus (FSI), contributing to various health benefits such as anti-cancer, antioxidant, antiviral, antithrombotic, analgesic, anti-aging, antibacterial, anti-inflammatory, and anti-allergic. This study developed a method to detect and identify characteristic compounds in Tartary buckwheat extracts and compared the key ingredients and biological activities of Tartary buckwheat and Flos Sophorae Immaturus.

pmc-13099331.title: Growth factor-free chondrogenesis and immunomodulation of Wharton’s jelly MSCs on chitosan-hyaluronic acid films
pmc-13099331.creator: Rasha Basso, Ahed Ghamrawi, Bayan Aasar, Khoder Ghassa, Nour Shakik, Mario Karam, Layal El-Hajjar, Marc Karam, Aline Nassar, Lara Haddad, Marwan El-Sabban, Zeina Nasr, Chaza Harmouch
pmc-13099331.description: This study explores a surface modification strategy that mimics the native cellular environment through the layer-by-layer assembly of natural polyelectrolytes. Specifically, we developed a multilayer matrix composed of 10 alternating layers of chitosan (a polycation) and hyaluronic acid (a polyanion), seeded with Wharton’s jelly mesenchymal stem cells (WJ-MSCs) derived from human umbilical cords.

pmc-13469224.title: Structural determinants of child undernutrition: contribution of women’s empowerment in India’s nutritional transition
pmc-13469224.creator: Bharti Singh, Shri K Singh, Deepanjali Vishwakarma
pmc-13469224.description: Objective:This study aims to investigate the impact of women’s empowerment on child undernutrition from 2006 to 2021 in India at the state, primary sampling unit and household levels.Design:This study uses repeated cross-sectional data from three rounds of the National Family Health Survey (NFHS). Child undernutrition is assessed using stunting, wasting and underweight indicators, with women’s empowerment as a key predictor.

pmc-13543810.title: Low lymphoma macrophage infiltration predicts poor outcomes for R-CHOP– but not Pola-R-CHP–treated patients with DLBCL
pmc-13543810.creator: Franck Morschhauser, Georg Lenz, Alex F Herrera, Christopher R Flowers, Marek Trněný, John M Burke, Jing-Zhou Hou, Philipp B Staber, Eliza A Hawkes, Koji Izutsu, Steven Le Gouill, David Belada, Alessandra Tucci, Mark Yan, Will Harris, Kai Lu, Christopher R Bolen, Jamie Hirata, Calvin Lee, Yanwen Jia
pmc-13543810.description: Key Points•Low M1 infiltration is the main immune-related negative prognostic factor for progression-free survival in anti-CD20 + CHOP–treated patients.•Pola-R-CHP activity appears largely independent of M1 macrophage enrichment or overall immune cell infiltration. Introduction Dissecting cellular heterogeneity in diffuse large B-cell lymphoma (DLBCL) and elucidating its role in disease biology and clinical treatment outcomes has been the focus of active investigation.

pmc-13661275.title: Seasonality of lake microbial denitrification and its sensitivity to climate warming
pmc-13661275.creator: Cameron M Callbeck, Alessandra Mazzoli, Tim J Paulus, Claudia Frey, Helmut Bürgmann, Carsten J Schubert, Moritz F Lehmann
pmc-13661275.description: Lakes are expected to experience longer summer stratification and shorter winter mixing due to climate-induced warming. These changes will impact biogeochemical cycles, but how shifts in mixing might influence lake nitrogen removal via denitrification remains unconstrained. Here we used 15N-tracer assays, molecular techniques and flux measurements to establish the seasonal dynamics of denitrification in a eutrophic lake in Switzerland.

pmc-13670808.title: GluK1-containing kainate receptor-dependent long-term depression in the anterior cingulate cortex modulates chronic pain
pmc-13670808.creator: Zhi-Xia Zhao, Ye Sun, Zi-Yuan Li, Jianxiong Wei, Teng Chen, Jingmin Che, Min Zhuo, Xu-Hui Li
pmc-13670808.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). BackgroundLong-term depression (LTD) is a pivotal form of synaptic plasticity in the central nervous system, yet its functions and cortical mechanisms remain unclear in chronic pain. Kainate receptors (KARs) are ionotropic glutamate receptors that regulate the release of both excitatory and inhibitory neurotransmitters in several brain areas, such as the anterior cingulate cortex (ACC), which is an important part of the brain for processing pain and emotions. KAR-dependent long-term potentiation (LTP) in the ACC has been proven to contribute to chronic pain.
